commits.message:
feat(docs): "Try it" opens any docs example in the playground (rich-playground-afk.4kh)

Every example that runs (static, silent, throws, live) carries a "Try it"
link in its output label. It opens the playground on the block as a program of
its own: the block, plus the imports it uses and every statement above it
that declares something it uses (the prelude's console, the page context's
lines, earlier blocks' declarations). Statements above it that change one of
those without printing come along too. docs/.vitepress/example-slice.ts cuts
it using the TypeScript checker's reading of the page's own program.

Checked at build time, per block: the program type-checks alone, and each
block that runs at build time, run as the playground runs it (Sucrase + the
live library), prints the bytes the page shows and ends the same way. Across
the site 206 of 242 executed blocks need nothing from above; all 242 pass.

A page run now fixes the time and a seeded Math.random for every program it
runs, so a block run twice (chain and Try it) agrees; console.log's timestamp
is the one read that differed.

Verified in Chromium (e2e/try-it.spec.ts): Try it on docs/panel.md lands on
the playground with the code and the same rows the page shows; on
docs/progress.md's live track() example, with the page context's doStep, and
the same final frame.

feat(docs): the playground page: editor, Run, terminal (rich-playground-afk.npl) (#238)

* test(e2e): poll the rows of a worker that did not start (rich-playground-afk.npl)

The run's state turns exited as the report is written, and xterm draws the
write a moment later, so reading the rows once raced the draw. It failed about
one run in three under the full e2e group, on master too.

* feat(docs): the playground page: editor, Run, terminal (rich-playground-afk.npl)

A Playground nav tab: a CodeMirror 6 editor beside the live terminal, above it
at phone width, running the editor's TypeScript on the live library.

- Run, or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter in the editor, runs the editor's program, replacing
  the run before; Stop ends one that has not ended.
- Every edit is written to the URL hash (docs/.vitepress/playground-hash.ts:
  deflate, base64url), so a link or a reload opens the same program. A hash it
  cannot read is reported and the start example opened.
- It opens on the first block of docs/introduction.md, served with the live
  library as virtual:rich-live/playground. That block is type-checked with no
  prelude or page context, so one that stops being a program on its own fails
  the build at its line. The library module is the one the live examples
  import, so the site ships it once.
- Editor colours are One Light / One Dark Pro as custom properties, so the
  editor follows the site's colour mode; the terminal takes the example themes.

Verified in Chromium (e2e/playground.spec.ts): reached from the nav, start
example runs, edit and rerun by button and shortcut, reload and a fresh context
restore the program, unreadable link reported, endless loop stopped, phone
stacking, light and dark terminal themes.

* fix(docs): the playground's link keeps up, and a failed start retries (rich-playground-afk.npl)

Review (/code-review high) of PR #238:
- The hash is written once typing pauses: one history write a keystroke is
  a burst Safari and Firefox refuse and Chrome drops.
- Edits, followed links and closing are ordered events; an encode or decode
  that lands after a later event is dropped, replacing the unordered chain.
- `opened: Opened | null` meant both "opening" and "failed"; it is a Phase
  union, and Run opens a playground that failed to, as RichLive's button does.
- A link failure clears once a write makes the address bar and editor agree.
- A link followed in the tab runs in the page's motion mode.
- The start block must be one its page runs to an end (not node/shape/throws).
- decodeProgram refuses to inflate past MAX_PROGRAM_BYTES; encode refuses the same.
- aria-keyshortcuts dropped: it named Control+Enter on a Mac, and the kbd
  in the button's name already says the shortcut.

* fix(docs): a link the browser refuses to write is reported, not thrown (rich-playground-afk.npl)

/code-review medium: replaceState ran in the success arm of then(ok, err), so
a browser's refusal (URL length cap) escaped as an unhandled rejection.
